content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary objective lacks estimand specification",
      "quote": "The primary objective of this study is to determine the confirmed ORR with vidutolimod in combination with cemiplimab.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.1.1 Primary Objective",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary objective is stated without a corresponding estimand, which is required by ICH M11 and SPIRIT 2025 to define the treatment effect, population, intercurrent events, and summary measure. The thin/missing list flags 'Primary Objective(s) and Associated Estimand(s)' as thin.",
      "fix": "Add a formal estimand for the primary endpoint, specifying the target population, intercurrent event strategy (e.g., treatment discontinuation), and population-level summary (e.g., proportion with confirmed ORR)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of ORR endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition does not specify the time window for confirmation (e.g., at least 4 weeks later) or how responses are confirmed, which is inconsistent with standard RECIST 1.1 practice and may lead to ambiguity in analysis.",
      "fix": "Clarify the confirmation requirement (e.g., repeat assessment no less than 4 weeks after initial response) and specify the analysis set (e.g., all treated subjects)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Contradictory statements on treatment duration",
      "quote": "All subjects will receive vidutolimod and cemiplimab according to the treatment schedule up to 2 years or until a reason for treatment discontinuation is reached.",
      "page": 49,
      "section": "3.1 Overall Study Design",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The text says treatment continues 'up to 2 years' but later states 'At the end of the treatment period (2 years), the Sponsor will not continue to provide supplied study treatment'—this is consistent, but the earlier phrase 'up to 2 years' could be misread as a maximum, while the protocol may intend a fixed 2-year period. Also, the synopsis is missing, so the intended duration is unclear.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether 2 years is a fixed treatment duration or a maximum, and specify if treatment can be extended beyond 2 years under any circumstances."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing trial stopping rules and end-of-trial definition",
      "quote": "At the end of the treatment period (2 years), the Sponsor will not continue to provide supplied study treatment to subjects/investigators unless the Sponsor chooses to extend the study.",
      "page": 49,
      "section": "3.1 Overall Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify trial stopping rules (e.g., for safety or futility) or define the end of trial (e.g., last subject last visit). The thin/missing list flags 'Trial Stopping Rules' and 'Start of Trial and End of Trial' as missing.",
      "fix": "Add a section on trial stopping rules (including safety stopping criteria) and define the end of trial as the last visit of the last subject or a specific date."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent dosing schedule for vidutolimod",
      "quote": "Vidutolimod 10 mg will be administered weekly for 7 doses, after which it will be administered Q3W until the subject meets a condition for discontinuation of study treatment.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3.1 Overall Study Design",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The text says 'weekly for 7 doses' but the schema (Figure 1) likely shows a different schedule (e.g., QW for 7 weeks then Q3W). The phrase 'weekly for 7 doses' could mean 7 consecutive weeks, but the schema may show a different pattern. Also, the first dose may be SC or IT, which is not reflected in the dosing schedule description.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact timing of the 7 weekly doses (e.g., W1D1, W2D1, ... W7D1) and ensure consistency with the schema."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing contraception and lifestyle restrictions",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are as follows: • AEs, SAEs, and AEs leading to discontinuation or death, and severity of AEs as assessed by the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events Version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol text provided does not include any contraception requirements or lifestyle restrictions, which are essential for a study involving investigational drugs with potential teratogenicity. The thin/missing list flags 'Contraception' and 'Lifestyle Restrictions' as missing.",
      "fix": "Add a section detailing contraception requirements for males and females of childbearing potential, and any lifestyle restrictions (e.g., alcohol, smoking, sexual activity)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent use of 'PD-1–blocking antibody' terminology",
      "quote": "Cohort A2: Subjects who have progressed while receiving a PD-1–blocking antibody or within 12 weeks of discontinuation",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3.1 Overall Study Design",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol uses 'PD-1–blocking antibody' in cohort descriptions but later states 'The PD-1–blocking antibody administered in this study is cemiplimab.' This is consistent, but the term 'PD-1–blocking antibody' is used generically for prior therapy, which may include PD-L1 inhibitors; the protocol should clarify whether prior PD-L1 inhibitors are allowed.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether prior PD-L1 inhibitor therapy is considered equivalent to PD-1 blockade for eligibility, and define the term consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing post-treatment access to intervention",
      "quote": "At the end of the treatment period (2 years), the Sponsor will not continue to provide supplied study treatment to subjects/investigators unless the Sponsor chooses to extend the study.",
      "page": 49,
      "section": "3.1 Overall Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that the Sponsor will not continue to provide treatment after 2 years, but it does not describe any mechanism for continued access to vidutolimod or cemiplimab after the trial, which is required by ICH M11 (Section 4.5). The thin/missing list flags 'Access to Trial Intervention After End of Trial' as missing.",
      "fix": "Add a statement on whether post-trial access to the investigational drugs will be provided, and if so, under what conditions (e.g., extension protocol, compassionate use)."
    }
  ]
}
